nodes.label: Authority Score
nodes.summary: Query-specific speaker authority: clipped weighted sum of six components (profession 0.15, education 0.10, committee 0.25, acts 0.20, interventions 0.25, role 0.05), time-decayed with 548-day half-life and coalition-crossing invalidation.
nodes.relevance: Core ranking signal for per-party expert selection; weights are expert-set, not learned, and no internal ablation exists.

nodes.label: Ideological Compass
nodes.summary: Per-query two-axis compass: gpt-4.1-mini generates pole pairs, embedded axis vectors are Gram-Schmidt orthogonalized, fragments are LLM stance-scored in [-1,1], party positions are shrunk means n/(n+3).
nodes.relevance: The system's most visible interpretive output; currently has no external validation against expert-coded party positions.

nodes.label: Citation Verification Pipeline
nodes.summary: CitationRegistry lifecycle (REGISTERED to RESOLVED/FAILED/ORPHANED) plus a deterministic no-LLM Citation Surgeon that enforces literal-substring verbatim quotes, nested-quote rejection, and a cos>=0.22 coherence gate.
nodes.relevance: Delivers Quote Fidelity = 1.00 by construction; the surrounding prose is not entailment-checked, which is the main open surface.

nodes.label: Multi-View Retrieval
nodes.summary: Dense channel (Neo4j vector index, top-200, 0.55 floor, out-of-domain gate) plus graph channel (EuroVoc/act matching, act-to-signatory-to-speech traversal). No BM25, reranker, HyDE, or RRF.
nodes.relevance: The retrieval architecture whose channel contributions have never been ablated; entity-heavy Italian parliamentary text is a prime hybrid-retrieval candidate.

nodes.label: Weighted Merger & Party Quota
nodes.summary: Convex score fusion (0.35 relevance, 0.25 salience, 0.20 coverage, 0.15 diversity, 0.05 authority) with per-speaker/party caps and a min-5-per-party quota that evicts over-represented parties.
nodes.relevance: The code-level fairness guarantee of the system; its balance-versus-relevance cost is untested.

nodes.label: Evaluation Harness
nodes.summary: Deterministic automated metrics (Group Quotation 0.97, Quote Fidelity 1.00, Completeness 0.99, Mean Authority 0.53) plus a 6-expert blind A/B vs NotebookLM (N=67, Wilcoxon + Holm-Bonferroni, nothing significant after correction).
nodes.relevance: No LLM-as-judge anywhere; the human study was underpowered under family correction and its Krippendorff alpha was very low.

nodes.label: Camera XIX Corpus
nodes.summary: Italian Chamber of Deputies, XIX legislature: 706 sessions, 46.9k speeches, 175k+ chunks, 35.8k acts, 17.3k roll calls, 6.9M individual votes from dati.camera.it SPARQL + Akoma Ntoso XML; RDF export on Zenodo (CC BY-SA 4.0) and HF.
nodes.relevance: Currently the only open machine-readable Camera XIX corpus found in the literature inventory.

nodes.label: Neo4j Knowledge Graph
nodes.summary: Single Neo4j instance as sole data layer: 13 node labels, 15 relationship types, native 1536-d vector + full-text index; hierarchy Session-Debate-Phase-Speech-Chunk with exact-substring chunk invariant and date-qualified memberships.
nodes.relevance: Structural attribution (Speech-SPOKEN_BY-Person) makes first-order quote attribution a database lookup rather than a prediction.

nodes.label: BasqueParl
nodes.summary: Bilingual Basque-Spanish parliamentary corpus (41k speeches, 14M words, 2012-2020). Headline finding: the chamber president produces 55% of speeches but only 5% of words, so all analyses are reported with and without president texts.
nodes.relevance: The cleanest published quantification of procedural dominance in turn counts; direct empirical motivation for filtering chair/procedural interventions in the authority score.

nodes.label: ParlaSent-BCS
nodes.summary: 2,600 sentiment-annotated parliamentary sentences (Bosnia, Croatia, Serbia) with a 6-level reduction-friendly schema; Krippendorff alpha 0.60 (6-class) / 0.745 (ternary) / 0.83 (binary); BERTic beats XLM-R by ~7.6 F1.
nodes.relevance: Template annotation protocol (double-annotate, alpha at multiple granularities, reconcile hard disagreements) and evidence that regional/domain models beat generic multilingual ones.

nodes.label: LLaMandement
nodes.summary: French government (DGFiP) LoRA-tuned Llama-2 13B for neutral summarization of legislative amendments; 15,397 amendment-summary pairs released; human eval only (10 drafters, 30 held-out amendments); deployed on the 2024 Finance Bill.
nodes.relevance: Closest real-world European deployment analog: neutral institutional gold data, expert-panel evaluation with a human self-rating ceiling, and bias delta-testing against the base model.

nodes.label: Knesset-DictaBERT
nodes.summary: MLM-only continued pretraining of DictaBERT on the Hebrew Knesset Corpus (384M tokens): perplexity 22.87 to 6.60, +4.5pp top-1 masked accuracy. No downstream, retrieval, or embedding evaluation at all.
nodes.relevance: Defines the exact gap ParliamentRAG's embedding ablation fills: parliamentary DAPT encoders exist but none has ever been evaluated on retrieval.

nodes.label: ParliaBench
nodes.summary: UK benchmark for conditioned parliamentary speech generation (447k ParlaMint-GB speeches) with novel metrics: embedding-centroid Political Spectrum Alignment, Party Alignment, and Cross-Context Stability = 100/(1+CV). Single 3.8B LLM judge, no human validation.
nodes.relevance: Source of the Stability metric (must be cited to ParliaBench) and of centroid-based compass validation ideas; its weaknesses (no external party ground truth, no factual grounding) are ParliamentRAG's differentiators.

nodes.label: PolicyBot
nodes.summary: Policy-document RAG demo: semantic chunking, gte-multilingual embeddings, HyDE + 5x multi-query fused with RRF, bge cross-encoder rerank, local Gemma generation. Citation display only, no verification; components chosen on proxy benchmarks; no end-to-end eval.
nodes.relevance: The architectural comparable that shows citation display + prompted grounding is the current policy-RAG baseline; ParliamentRAG already implements the verification PolicyBot lists as future work.

nodes.label: ParlaCAP
nodes.summary: GPT-4o teacher (~$100 for 35k speeches) trains an XLM-R-Parla student to label ~8M ParlaMint speeches across 28 parliaments with 22 CAP major topics; human-LLM Krippendorff alpha 0.60-0.64 vs inter-human 0.59-0.68; Italian slice is Senate-only and unvalidated.
nodes.relevance: Hands ParliamentRAG a ready CAP topic layer (labels, prompt, classifier) plus the replicable teacher-student validation protocol; Italian gold test data remains to be built.

nodes.label: Proksch & Slapin 2012
nodes.summary: Canonical comparative theory of legislative speech: floor access is strategically allocated by party rules (electoral system, candidate selection), not a neutral reflection of expertise.
nodes.relevance: Questions intervention counts as an expertise proxy and supports keeping interventions as one of six fused signals; motivates conditioning on party and role.

nodes.label: Politics of Parliamentary Debate (2015)
nodes.summary: Book-length delegation model of speaking time between leaders and backbenchers with cross-national empirics; debate participation tracks party discipline and electoral incentives.
nodes.relevance: Italy's group-allocated speaking time means intervention volume carries party-size and role confounds that per-speaker normalization does not remove.

nodes.label: Back, Debus & Muller 2014
nodes.summary: Swedish Riksdag study: female MPs give fewer speeches, especially in 'hard' policy debates, controlling for seniority and committee assignment.
nodes.relevance: Warns that activity-based authority inherits participation biases; supports demographic sanity checks on authority distributions.

nodes.label: Fernandes, Debus & Back 2021
nodes.summary: State-of-the-field review of legislative debate research: what debates are for, who speaks, and under which institutional constraints.
nodes.relevance: The umbrella citation for 'speech participation is strategically allocated and cannot be read as raw expertise', motivating the multi-component authority design.

nodes.label: Quinn et al. 2010
nodes.summary: Dynamic topic model over US Senate speech establishing per-legislator topic-attention profiles as meaningful quantities; attention tracks committee duties.
nodes.relevance: Closest political-science ancestor of the topic-conditioned interventions component; supports topic-weighted speech counts over raw counts.

nodes.label: Get Out the Vote (2006)
nodes.summary: First influential coupling of floor-speech text with relational structure (agreement links) for vote prediction via collective classification; introduces the ConVote corpus.
nodes.relevance: Conceptual ancestor of speech/vote/speaker graph reasoning and of any vote-supervised stance component over ParliamentRAG's roll-call graph.

nodes.label: Abercrombie & Batista-Navarro survey
nodes.summary: Systematic review of 61 studies on sentiment and position-taking in parliamentary debates, cataloguing preprocessing conventions and the sentiment/stance split.
nodes.relevance: Best single entry point for situating the compass; documents that procedural filtering is standard practice in this literature.

nodes.label: HITS (Kleinberg 1999)
nodes.summary: Defines authority as an emergent property of a mutually reinforcing hub-authority link structure computed per query-focused subgraph: authority is topic-conditional.
nodes.relevance: Places ParliamentRAG's query-conditioned score in the HITS tradition, and highlights the missing endorsement dimension (who cites/mentions whom).

nodes.label: PageRank (Brin & Page 1998)
nodes.summary: Global recursive endorsement-based importance over a link graph; query-independent counterpart to HITS.
nodes.relevance: A PageRank over ParliamentRAG's MENTIONS/CITES/co-signature graph could replace the flat 0.3 base prior in the role component.

nodes.label: TREC 2005 Enterprise Track
nodes.summary: Established expert finding as a benchmarked task: rank people by topical expertise, with organizational working-group membership as ground truth.
nodes.relevance: Template for validating per-party expert selection: committee membership is the parliamentary analogue of working-group ground truth.

nodes.label: Balog et al. 2006
nodes.summary: Two generative expert-finding models: candidate-centric (person = their documents) and document-centric (credit people via topic-relevant documents); association strength is the key modeling choice.
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG's interventions/acts components are Model-1-style; Model 2 suggests scoring authority from the retrieved pool itself; validates PRIMARY 1.0 vs CO 0.3 signature weighting.

nodes.label: Expertise Retrieval survey (2012)
nodes.summary: Comprehensive survey grouping expertise-retrieval approaches into five families and covering evidence beyond documents: position, social ties, temporal dynamics.
nodes.relevance: The best citation framing the authority score as a standard voting/fusion combination of heterogeneous expertise evidence.

nodes.label: Author-Topic Model (2004)
nodes.summary: Each author is a learned distribution over topics from their documents, enabling who-writes-about-what queries.
nodes.relevance: Probabilistic ancestor of the per-speaker topical profile; suggests precomputed per-deputy topic distributions as a cheaper alternative to per-query scoring.

nodes.label: Expertise Networks (Zhang et al. 2007)
nodes.summary: ExpertiseRank (PageRank variant) versus simple measures on the Java Forum: graph-recursive algorithms did not beat simple degree-style counts; performance depends on network structure.
nodes.relevance: Caution that any future endorsement-based authority component must be benchmarked against the simple activity components first.

nodes.label: TwitterRank (2010)
nodes.summary: Topic-sensitive PageRank with transition probabilities weighted by content similarity between users; influence is computed per topic and beats global PageRank.
nodes.relevance: Clearest published precedent for ParliamentRAG's central design decision that influence must be topic-conditional, combining structure with content similarity.

nodes.label: Connecting the Congress (Fowler 2006)
nodes.summary: Cosponsorship networks from ~280k US bills; 'connectedness' centrality weighting cosponsorship predicts legislative influence outcomes.
nodes.relevance: Direct validation for the acts component's use of the signature graph, and the natural external-validation covariate (Fowler-style connectedness on PRIMARY/CO_SIGNATORY edges).

nodes.label: House committee networks (2005)
nodes.summary: Committee-committee networks via membership interlocks in the US House recover hierarchical and political structure from membership alone.
nodes.relevance: Supports the committee component's premise that membership encodes real topical structure; suggests interlock embeddings as a check on curated YAML topics.

nodes.label: Italian Chamber voting network (2014)
nodes.summary: Co-voting similarity network over deputies of the Italian Chamber of Deputies; community detection recovers coalitions and quantifies cohesion and government strength.
nodes.relevance: Proof that ParliamentRAG's 6.9M votes support deputy-level network analysis in this exact chamber, and grounding for the coalition-crossing invalidation logic.

nodes.label: Card et al. 2022 (procedural classifier)
nodes.summary: 140-year Congressional Record study that trains classifiers to identify and exclude procedural speeches (rules, vote announcements, turn management) before substantive analysis.
nodes.relevance: The concrete citable supervised methodology for procedural filtering of the interventions component.

nodes.label: Aroyehun et al. 2025
nodes.summary: Nature Human Behaviour study over ~8M congressional speeches; removes procedural speeches with a majority-vote ensemble of three classifiers following Card et al. before any text measure.
nodes.relevance: Strongest recent top-venue precedent that procedural filtering is required hygiene before per-speaker text aggregates.

nodes.label: Aroyehun et al. 2026 (preprint)
nodes.summary: 15M speech segments across 7 countries (1946-2025); chair-speech removal and LLM-rated procedural filtering feed an Evidence-Minus-Intuition score.
nodes.relevance: Frontier practice: an index-time LLM procedural rating is the lowest-engineering-cost filtering option for ParliamentRAG's existing stack.

nodes.label: Mining Ethos (Duthie et al. 2016)
nodes.summary: Annotates and automatically recognizes ethotic expressions (support/attack on a speaker's character) in Hansard, with polarity.
nodes.relevance: Ethos mining yields a text-derived endorsement graph: the missing 'reputation among peers' dimension of the authority score.

nodes.label: Krehbiel 1991
nodes.summary: The informational theory of legislative organization: committees exist so legislators specialize and acquire policy expertise the chamber then exploits.
nodes.relevance: THE theoretical justification for the committee component (weight 0.25) and for committee-officer bonuses in the role component.

nodes.label: Legislative Effectiveness (2014)
nodes.summary: Defines the Legislative Effectiveness Score: a per-legislator composite over bill-progression stages times significance tiers, normalized per Congress.
nodes.relevance: Closest existing validated composite per-legislator score; suggests adding act-outcome stages to the acts component and serves as an external validation target.

nodes.label: T-Rank (2005)
nodes.summary: Extends PageRank with temporal freshness and activity of pages and links; authority flows preferentially through fresh, active edges.
nodes.relevance: Direct precedent for exponential time decay in authority computation; suggests separating 'recently active' from 'long-run specialist', which one half-life conflates.

nodes.label: Temporal Expertise Profiling (2014)
nodes.summary: Models a person's expertise as a time series of hierarchical topic-profile snapshots with change detection.
nodes.relevance: Validates date-parameterized authority and coalition-period filtering; suggests exposing per-deputy authority trajectories as a consistency check.

nodes.label: Echoes of Power (2012)
nodes.summary: Power differentials are detectable from linguistic coordination: lower-power participants echo the function-word style of higher-power ones (Wikipedia, US Supreme Court).
nodes.relevance: Offers a purely text-derived, activity-independent power signal for external validation of the authority score.

nodes.label: AIS (Rashkin et al. 2023)
nodes.summary: Defines Attributable to Identified Sources: output y is attributable to source P iff a generic hearer would affirm 'According to P, y'; two-stage human protocol with an interpretability step.
nodes.relevance: Conceptual root of ParliamentRAG's guarantee: the substring check is a deterministic sufficient condition for AIS on quote spans, and AIS names what it does not cover (the surrounding prose).

nodes.label: Attributed QA / AutoAIS
nodes.summary: Formulates attributed QA and proposes AutoAIS: an NLI model predicting whether the cited passage entails the answer, correlating with human AIS at system level (~0.96 reported).
nodes.relevance: AutoAIS is exactly the prose-entailment half ParliamentRAG lacks; the cos>=0.22 coherence gate is a lightweight surrogate for it.

nodes.label: Attribution/Citation/Quotation survey
nodes.summary: Systematizes 134 papers and ~300 metrics; separates citation (marker), attribution (output-evidence link), and quotation (verbatim reuse); only 13% of papers quote at all.
nodes.relevance: Best framing citation: ParliamentRAG occupies the nearly empty intersection of all three paradigms.

nodes.label: WebGPT
nodes.summary: GPT-3 fine-tuned to browse with an explicit quote action clipping verbatim extracts into a reference buffer; answers cite references by index; RLHF-trained.
nodes.relevance: Guarantees a verbatim reference pool but only encourages answer-to-reference fidelity; ParliamentRAG closes that gap with the substring-checked quote in the answer itself.

nodes.label: GopherCite
nodes.summary: 280B model trained (SFT + RLHF) to answer with claim + source + quoted passage; Supported & Plausible 80% (NQ) / 67% (ELI5), human-verified; verbatimness is a trained tendency, not a guarantee.
nodes.relevance: The closest neighbor and sharpest contrast: learned quoting verified at 67-80% by humans versus ParliamentRAG's deterministic post-condition (QF = 1.00 by construction).

nodes.label: 'According to...' / QUIP-Score
nodes.summary: Grounding phrases increase verbatim overlap with a trusted corpus; QUIP-Score measures character n-gram membership via a Bloom-filter index; higher QUIP correlates with fewer hallucinations.
nodes.relevance: Metric-space analog of the surgeon: Quote Fidelity is effectively QUIP = 1.0 enforced on designated quote spans rather than measured on free text.

nodes.label: Quote-Tuning
nodes.summary: DPO alignment toward verbatim quoting scored by Bloom-filter corpus membership: up to ~130% relative quoting increase with maintained quality; 'verifiable by design' thesis.
nodes.relevance: Strongest peer-reviewed argument that verbatim quotation is a verifiability feature; ParliamentRAG achieves it architecturally at inference without fine-tuning.

nodes.label: NEST (speculative span splicing)
nodes.summary: Token-level kNN retrieval with speculative acceptance of retrieved corpus spans; accepted spans are real corpus text so span-level attribution comes free; 1.8x speedup.
nodes.relevance: The decoding-level extreme of copying spans instead of citing; ParliamentRAG keeps quotes reader-visible and verified post hoc with graph attribution.

nodes.label: Attribute First, then Generate
nodes.summary: Decomposes generation into span selection, sentence planning, and per-sentence fusion of only the selected spans, giving span-level attribution by construction.
nodes.relevance: Closest architectural relative to the staged pipeline; its sentences are still abstractive fusions, whereas ParliamentRAG's quote spans are verbatim and machine-verified.

nodes.label: ReClaim
nodes.summary: Interleaves verbatim reference spans with claim sentences; reports ~90% citation accuracy, measured, not guaranteed.
nodes.relevance: The measured-90% versus enforced-100% contrast is exactly the surgeon's contribution.

nodes.label: VeriCite
nodes.summary: Per-claim NLI verification during generation, evidence selection, then LLM refinement rewriting the answer with verified citations; all verification is semantic, no substring guarantee.
nodes.relevance: State-of-the-art NLI-side pipeline and the natural head-to-head baseline: VeriCite verifies claims but not quotes, ParliamentRAG verifies quotes but not claims.

nodes.label: FRONT
nodes.summary: Grounds outputs in fine-grained supporting quotes before generating; improves ALCE citation quality by ~14% on LLaMA-2-7B, surpassing ChatGPT.
nodes.relevance: Published evidence that quote-first grounding improves NLI-measured citation quality, supporting the evidence-first design; still evaluated with NLI metrics.

nodes.label: ALCE
nodes.summary: The canonical citation-evaluation benchmark: NLI-based citation recall (cited passages entail the statement) and precision (leave-one-out irrelevance test); best models lack complete support ~50% of the time on ELI5.
nodes.relevance: The reference metric suite ParliamentRAG must be positioned against: QF = 1.00 does not measure ALCE-style prose-statement support.

nodes.label: RARR
nodes.summary: Post-hoc research-and-revise: retrieve evidence for any generator's output, minimally edit unsupported content, emit an attribution report; measures attribution-preservation trade-off.
nodes.relevance: Archetype of post-hoc revision; ParliamentRAG's EvidenceFirstWriter repair fallback is a constrained cousin.

nodes.label: L-CiteEval
nodes.summary: Long-context citation benchmark (8K-48K): citation fidelity degrades with context length; open models trail closed ones, suggesting parametric answering over context grounding.
nodes.relevance: Parliamentary sessions are long documents; motivates reporting ParliamentRAG citation metrics as a function of retrieved-context size (top-k = 200).

nodes.label: Verifiability of generative search engines
nodes.summary: Human audit of Bing Chat, NeevaAI, perplexity.ai, YouChat: only 51.5% of sentences fully supported by citations, 74.5% citation precision; fluency inversely correlates with citation quality.
nodes.relevance: Established citation recall/precision for deployed systems; the 'fluent but unsupported' risk is what the substring constraint eliminates for quote spans.

nodes.label: Correctness is not Faithfulness
nodes.summary: Splits citation correctness (cited document entails statement) from citation faithfulness (the model causally relied on it); up to ~57% of citations lack faithfulness even when correct.
nodes.relevance: Sharpest scoping tool for the QF = 1.00 claim: verbatim quotes prove correctness of quoted material, not causal reliance or the surrounding claims.

nodes.label: AttrScore
nodes.summary: Replaces binary entailment with a 3-way attributable / extrapolatory / contradictory scheme for finer attribution error identification.
nodes.relevance: Extrapolatory framing (unsupported interpretation of a real quote) is the dominant political failure mode; the 3-way schema fits ParliamentRAG's prose verification better than binary NLI.

nodes.label: AttributionBench
nodes.summary: Unifies attribution datasets; even fine-tuned GPT-3.5 reaches only ~80% macro-F1 on binary attributability.
nodes.relevance: Any NLI/LLM judge added for prose entailment is itself ~80%-reliable, strengthening the case for deterministic substring checks wherever they apply.

nodes.label: Fabricated references study
nodes.summary: 636 ChatGPT-generated citations audited: 55% of GPT-3.5 references fabricated versus 18% for GPT-4; many real ones contain substantive errors.
nodes.relevance: Standard motivation citation: ParliamentRAG's citations are constructed from retrieved graph records, making fabricated references structurally impossible.

nodes.label: Hallucination snowballing
nodes.summary: LMs over-commit to early mistakes and generate further false claims they can separately recognize as wrong (self-recognition 67-94%).
nodes.relevance: Why per-statement verification matters even with verbatim quotes: one unsupported framing claim can snowball through a party-position summary.

nodes.label: LLM hallucination survey (TOIS)
nodes.summary: LLM-era canonical survey: factuality versus faithfulness hallucination, causes across data/training/inference, and RAG-specific 'context-inconsistency'.
nodes.relevance: Context-inconsistency names exactly what remains unchecked in ParliamentRAG's connective prose; QF covers a narrow slice of the faithfulness taxonomy.

nodes.label: SummaC
nodes.summary: NLI entailment matrix over document x summary sentences; granularity fix lifts NLI inconsistency detection to 72-74% balanced accuracy; thresholds require per-dataset calibration.
nodes.relevance: Best-fit design for the missing prose layer: chunk sentences as premises, each prose sentence as hypothesis, with max-aggregation identifying the supporting chunk for automatic citation binding.

nodes.label: QAFactEval
nodes.summary: Component-optimized QA-based factual-consistency pipeline reaching 77.8% balanced accuracy; shows QA and NLI signals are complementary.
nodes.relevance: Supports layering QA probes on top of an NLI gate; all components are English-trained, so an Italian port needs new QG/QA models.

nodes.label: FActScore
nodes.summary: Decomposes long-form generations into atomic facts (LLM-drafted; humans revised ~52% of them) verified against retrieved passages; score = fraction supported.
nodes.relevance: Per-claim verification is more diagnostic than per-sentence for multi-claim political prose; the 52% revision rate warns the decomposer itself needs validation.

nodes.label: AlignScore
nodes.summary: Single 355M alignment function trained on 4.7M examples from 7 task families; matches or beats ChatGPT/GPT-4 judges on 22 factual-consistency datasets.
nodes.relevance: Best quality-per-parameter candidate for a self-hosted deterministic prose-verification layer; English-trained, so Italian needs a multilingual variant.

nodes.label: Self-RAG
nodes.summary: Fine-tunes an LM to emit reflection tokens including ISSUP (segment fully/partially/not supported by passage), enabling decoding-time faithfulness control.
nodes.relevance: ISSUP is a built-in per-segment support check of the kind ParliamentRAG's prose lacks; the reusable part is the support-label schema for a post-hoc checker.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Verification
nodes.summary: Draft, plan verification questions, answer them independently (withholding the draft to avoid sycophancy), then revise; factored variants win.
nodes.relevance: Cheapest prototype of a prose-verification loop; the withhold-the-draft lesson applies to any LLM-judge configuration.

nodes.label: RAGAS
nodes.summary: Reference-free LLM-judged RAG metrics (faithfulness by statement decomposition, answer and context relevance); the paper's entire human validation is 50 synthetic Wikipedia items.
nodes.relevance: Language-flexible (so Italian-capable) faithfulness harness, but its scores are unvalidated for Italian parliamentary text and inherit judge noise.

nodes.label: Why Language Models Hallucinate
nodes.summary: Statistical account: hallucinations are ordinary errors of an implicit valid/invalid classifier, and post-training worsens them because benchmarks reward confident guessing.
nodes.relevance: Motivates system-level guarantees (deterministic substring check plus entailment layer) as the principled mitigation path since model-level elimination is not available.

nodes.label: Pointer-Generator Networks
nodes.summary: Per-step soft interpolation between vocabulary generation and copying source tokens via attention; copying is probabilistic, with no phrase-level verbatim guarantee.
nodes.relevance: The canonical copy-mechanism ancestor; the surgeon is its hard deterministic descendant (verify substrings post hoc instead of biasing generation).

nodes.label: SEAL (autoregressive search)
nodes.summary: BART + FM-index constrained decoding: only continuations that exist verbatim in the corpus can be emitted, so generated n-grams are guaranteed attested substrings; ~10 points over retrievers on KILT.
nodes.relevance: Proves corpus-scale exact-substring-constrained decoding is feasible: the generation-time dual of ParliamentRAG's post-hoc check, already cited in its future work.

nodes.label: CAMS (claim-anchored provenance)
nodes.summary: Multi-document summarization with provenance resolved deterministically from verbatim quotes to token spans; faithfulness of surrounding text is encouraged, not NLI-gated; no metadata graph.
nodes.relevance: The nearest published hybrid to ParliamentRAG's design and the key defensive citation for the verbatim+entailment novelty claim.

nodes.label: Speaker attribution in Bundestag debates
nodes.summary: GePaDe_SpkAtt: 7,700+ annotated speech/thought/writing events in Bundestag debates with source/addressee/message roles; attribution treated as a learned prediction problem.
nodes.relevance: Shows who-said-what within an utterance (reported speech) is nontrivial even in parliaments: the literature anchor for the surgeon's nested-third-party-quote rejection.

nodes.label: Towards Fair RAG (Kim & Diaz)
nodes.summary: First systematic evaluation of RAG with exposure-fair stochastic retrievers across 12 models / 7 tasks; distinguishes ranking fairness from attribution fairness (exposure of sources actually cited); fair retrieval often maintains or improves quality.
nodes.relevance: Central RAG-fairness reference: validates the bet that coverage/diversity terms need not cost quality, and supplies the retrieval-share vs citation-share audit distinction.

nodes.label: ARES
nodes.summary: Synthetic-data-fine-tuned lightweight RAG judges anchored by prediction-powered inference on a small human-labeled set, yielding statistically corrected confidence intervals.
nodes.relevance: The most important methodological template: ParliamentRAG's 67 expert judgments are exactly the PPI anchor, though below the recommended few hundred labels.

nodes.label: RGB benchmark
nodes.summary: Benchmarks four RAG abilities with largely deterministic scoring: noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, counterfactual robustness; LLMs struggle at rejection and integration.
nodes.relevance: Proof that meaningful RAG failure modes are measurable without an LLM judge; maps onto ParliamentRAG's unevaluated out-of-domain gate.

nodes.label: CRAG benchmark (Meta)
nodes.summary: 4,409 QA pairs, 5 domains, mock web + KG search APIs; correct/missing/hallucinated scoring; SOTA industry RAG at most 63% hallucination-free, worst on dynamic facts and tail entities.
nodes.relevance: Its KG+text hybrid mirrors ParliamentRAG's channels and its question-type taxonomy suggests harder query templates than the single position-question template.

nodes.label: GroUSE
nodes.summary: 144 unit tests probing whether judges detect 7 grounded-QA failure modes; RAGAS/DeepEval-style pipelines overlook important failures even with GPT-4; judge-judge correlation is a misleading validity proxy.
nodes.relevance: Peer-reviewed ammunition that bolting on an LLM judge is not automatically more valid than deterministic checks; any ParliamentRAG judge should pass adapted unit tests first.

nodes.label: RAGChecker
nodes.summary: Claim-level entailment decomposition of answers and ground truths into diagnostic retriever metrics (claim recall, context precision) and generator metrics (faithfulness, noise sensitivity, hallucination).
nodes.relevance: The natural middle ground: quotes stay deterministically verified, non-quote prose gets claim-level NLI checking.

nodes.label: LLM-as-a-Judge (MT-Bench)
nodes.summary: Canonical LLM-judge paper: GPT-4 matches human preferences at >80% agreement (human-human level); documents position, verbosity, and self-enhancement bias with mitigations.
nodes.relevance: The license for LLM judging at all and the original documentation of self-enhancement, the reason a GPT judge over GPT outputs needs controls.

nodes.label: LLM evaluators favor their own generations
nodes.summary: GPT-4/Llama-2 recognize their own outputs out of the box; fine-tuning shows a linear link between self-recognition capability and self-preference strength: a causal recognition-to-preference route.
nodes.relevance: Decisive: the bias is style-recognition-driven and not removable by prompting, arguing directly for a cross-family judge for GPT-4o outputs.

nodes.label: LLMs are not fair evaluators
nodes.summary: Pairwise verdicts hackable by response order alone: Vicuna-13B 'beats' ChatGPT on 66/80 queries purely via ordering; proposes balanced position calibration.
nodes.relevance: Any ParliamentRAG judge run on A/B pairs must score both orderings and aggregate, since position bias can exceed the true effect size (~d=0.3).

nodes.label: G-Eval
nodes.summary: CoT + form-filling GPT-4 evaluator with strong human correlation gains; the authors themselves flag its bias toward LLM-generated text over human-written text.
nodes.relevance: Even a well-designed rubric judge inherits LLM-text preference; absolute rubric scores are less trustworthy than human-anchored pairwise comparisons.

nodes.label: PoLL (Panel of LLM evaluators)
nodes.summary: A panel of small judges from disjoint model families outperforms a single GPT-4 judge in human correlation, mitigates intra-model bias, and is >7x cheaper.
nodes.relevance: The direct design template for ParliamentRAG's judge: 3 small judges from 3 families with vote pooling, weighted away from the generator's family.

nodes.label: Self-preference bias mechanism
nodes.summary: Judges over-score low-perplexity (familiar) text relative to humans, independent of literal self-generation.
nodes.relevance: Generalizes self-preference to same-family outputs: a GPT judge is familiarity-biased toward GPT-4o siblings even without producing the text.

nodes.label: Preference Leakage
nodes.summary: Formalizes generator-judge relatedness (same model, distilled, same family) and shows systematic bias toward related models; contamination is harder to detect than position or verbosity bias.
nodes.relevance: Closest peer-reviewed match to 'GPT judging GPT': primary citation justifying a cross-family judge for GPT-4o/4.1 generations.

nodes.label: JudgeBench
nodes.summary: On deliberately hard pairs where factual correctness decides the winner, strong judges including GPT-4o are barely above random (~50%).
nodes.relevance: Keep factual checks retrieval-grounded and deterministic; the judge should own only holistic preference and prose quality.

nodes.label: AutoEval Done Right (PPI)
nodes.summary: PPI-family estimators combine LLM-judge labels with a small human-labeled set into unbiased comparisons, stretching effective human-sample size by up to ~50%.
nodes.relevance: With 67 human pairs as anchor, judge bias (including family bias) is corrected in expectation with honest confidence intervals.

nodes.label: Human NLG eval best practices
nodes.summary: Field survey of human NLG evaluation: Likert dominance, minority IAA and significance reporting; recommends more raters, mandatory agreement statistics, full protocol documentation.
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG's study exceeds field norms on reporting; its low alpha is consistent with field-wide subjective-criterion agreement.

nodes.label: Twenty Years of Confusion
nodes.summary: 165 NLG papers use 200+ distinct, mostly undefined quality-criterion names; proposes standardized definitions and evaluation sheets.
nodes.relevance: Nine Likert dimensions with near-zero alpha is the textbook symptom of criterion ambiguity; the redesign should cut to <=4 sheet-defined criteria.

nodes.label: With Little Power (Card et al.)
nodes.summary: Meta-analysis of NLP human evaluations: the modal design (3 annotators x 100 items) is underpowered unless the true effect exceeds ~0.2; recommends prospective power analysis and mixed-effects models.
nodes.relevance: The direct explanation of ParliamentRAG's null result: 6 raters x 67 pairs under 9-way correction was underpowered for every observed effect size.

nodes.label: Equivalence tests primer (TOST)
nodes.summary: Practical primer for two one-sided equivalence tests: pre-specify the smallest effect size of interest and reject both one-sided nulls to claim equivalence.
nodes.relevance: The only way to convert 'nothing significant' into an affirmative non-inferiority/equivalence claim for ParliamentRAG vs NotebookLM and for party-parity claims.

nodes.label: Best-Worst Scaling reliability
nodes.summary: At equal annotation budget, best-worst scaling is far more reliable than rating scales, which suffer scale-interpretation inconsistency and region bias.
nodes.relevance: Validates the comparative A/B arm of the existing study and indicts the 9 absolute Likert dimensions as the weak link.

nodes.label: LLM relevance judgment perspectives
nodes.summary: Position paper defining the human-machine collaboration spectrum for relevance judgments, with cautions on prompt sensitivity and circularity.
nodes.relevance: Names 'pooling + LLM qrels + small human validation' as an endorsed mid-spectrum strategy, not a shortcut.

nodes.label: LLMs predict searcher preferences
nodes.summary: GPT-4 relevance labels reach kappa 0.64 vs NIST (best prompt), exceeding trained inter-assessor agreement (0.52); in Bing production since 2022 at ~1/20 crowd cost; kappa swings 0.2+ across paraphrases.
nodes.relevance: Sets acceptance thresholds for an Italian parliamentary LLM assessor and prescribes the role of a small expert sample: prompt selection and monitoring.

nodes.label: UMBRELA
nodes.summary: Open reproduction of LLM relevance assessment with GPT-4o: modest per-label kappa (0.42-0.50 binarized) but near-perfect system-ranking correlation (Kendall tau 0.87-0.94); used for TREC 2024 RAG.
nodes.relevance: The tool to run over pooled ParliamentRAG chunks: modest label agreement still suffices for comparing retriever configurations.

nodes.label: TREC 2024 RAG / AutoNuggetizer
nodes.summary: Revives nugget-based evaluation for RAG: LLM-drafted nuggets from pooled evidence, support labels per answer; run-level Kendall tau 0.783 automatic vs manual, noisier per topic.
nodes.relevance: SOTA template for the end-to-end answer axis: LLM-drafted nuggets plus light expert editing over the policy topics.

nodes.label: Voorhees 2000 (assessor variation)
nodes.summary: Absolute retrieval scores shift with the assessor, but relative system orderings are stable across assessors' qrels (Kendall tau ~0.94).
nodes.relevance: Theoretical license for pooling + one consistent (LLM) assessor to rank ParliamentRAG retriever variants correctly.

nodes.label: Don't use LLMs for relevance judgments
nodes.summary: Position: LLM-authored truth data collapses retrieval and evaluation into one problem and sets that LLM as a performance ceiling; LLMs may assist but final judgments should stay human-grounded.
nodes.relevance: The caution requiring the collection be labeled 'LLM-assisted qrels, human-audited', never 'ground truth'.

nodes.label: LLM judgments can't replace humans
nodes.summary: Critique of LLM relevance assessment: circularity (LLM judges can favor systems built on similar LLMs), leaderboard correlation is insufficient validity evidence, prompt sensitivity.
nodes.relevance: The qrel judge for retrieval ablations should differ from the generation family even though retrieval-only comparisons carry lower circularity risk.

nodes.label: BM25 monograph (Robertson & Zaragoza)
nodes.summary: Canonical modern statement of BM25/BM25F derived from the probabilistic relevance framework.
nodes.relevance: The theoretical anchor for adding a sparse leg: parliamentary discourse is dense with exact-match signals (act numbers, names, EuroVoc terms).

nodes.label: BEIR
nodes.summary: Zero-shot heterogeneous retrieval benchmark (18 datasets): BM25 is a robust OOD baseline, dense models often underperform it out of domain, cross-encoders generalize best; in-domain rank does not predict transfer. No parliamentary collection exists in it.
nodes.relevance: Two lessons for the ablation: always include a BM25 arm, and the DAPT arm must beat a strong generic baseline; also confirms the parliamentary-benchmark gap.

nodes.label: EntityQuestions (Sciavolino et al.)
nodes.summary: Simple entity-centric questions make dense retrievers (DPR) drastically underperform BM25; dense models generalize only to common entities.
nodes.relevance: Most direct evidence that a dense-only channel will miss rare-entity queries; ParliamentRAG queries are heavily entity-centric (deputies, bills, parties).

nodes.label: DPR (Karpukhin et al.)
nodes.summary: Dual-encoder trained with in-batch negatives beats BM25 by 9-19 points top-20 accuracy on open QA; established dense retrieval as practical.
nodes.relevance: Origin of the architecture behind ParliamentRAG's dense channel; the DPR-BEIR-EntityQuestions arc is why dense-only is not enough.

nodes.label: Sentence-BERT
nodes.summary: Siamese/triplet fine-tuning makes BERT embeddings cosine-comparable; the recipe (pooling + contrastive fine-tuning) that turns any MLM into a retriever.
nodes.relevance: Exactly what an XLM-R-Parla-derived embedding arm requires: parliamentary MLMs must be SBERT-ified before serving the dense channel.

nodes.label: DPR replication (hybrid evidence)
nodes.summary: DPR's BM25 baseline was under-tuned; with a proper baseline, an alpha-weighted dense+BM25 hybrid consistently beats both single channels.
nodes.relevance: Directly supports the hybrid hypothesis and provides the simplest hybrid scoring form to compare against RRF.

nodes.label: Fusion function analysis (Bruch et al.)
nodes.summary: Systematic comparison of convex score combination vs RRF: a tuned convex combination outperforms RRF in- and out-of-domain, and is robust to normalization choice.
nodes.relevance: Key modern result defending ParliamentRAG's convex merger over RRF, provided the weights are tuned, which they currently are not.

nodes.label: Dense retrievers require BM25 interpolation
nodes.summary: Dense retrievers encode strong relevance signals but miss weaker ones; BM25 interpolation recovers them with significant gains, unlike for rerankers.
nodes.relevance: Predicts BM25 will add most value in ParliamentRAG's mid-rank region, exactly where the min-per-party quota pulls evidence from.

nodes.label: Sparse, dense, attentional representations
nodes.summary: Theory: fixed-length dense encodings have capacity limits growing with document length; sparse-dense hybrids capture sparse precision plus dense recall.
nodes.relevance: Theoretical grounding for the hybrid arm and for ParliamentRAG's chunk-level (not speech-level) embedding design.

nodes.label: CombSUM/CombMNZ (Fox & Shaw)
nodes.summary: Introduced CombSUM (sum of normalized scores) and CombMNZ: the origin of score-level fusion.
nodes.relevance: The correct ancestor for ParliamentRAG's weighted merger, which descends from the CombSUM family rather than from RRF.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
nodes.summary: RRF score = sum over rankings of 1/(k + rank), k=60; rank-based, scale-free fusion that beat every individual system and Condorcet fusion on TREC runs.
nodes.relevance: The standard fusion ParliamentRAG deliberately does not use; the natural baseline for the fusion ablation and for adding a BM25 leg without score calibration.

nodes.label: MMR (Carbonell & Goldstein)
nodes.summary: Maximal Marginal Relevance: greedy selection trading query relevance against redundancy with already-selected items.
nodes.relevance: Direct ancestor of the merger's diversity/coverage penalties, which are MMR variants with categorical (speaker/party) instead of content similarity.

nodes.label: xQuAD (Santos et al.)
nodes.summary: Explicit diversification: model the query's aspects and greedily maximize coverage of uncovered aspects, versus MMR's implicit dissimilarity.
nodes.relevance: The per-party quota is explicit diversification with exogenous known aspects (the party system); party_coverage is an aspect-recall analogue.

nodes.label: HyDE (Gao et al.)
nodes.summary: LLM generates a hypothetical answer document whose embedding retrieves real documents; gains demonstrated zero-shot with unsupervised encoders, shrinking with stronger retrievers.
nodes.relevance: For ParliamentRAG the prior is weak or negative: an in-domain gated dense channel is the strong-retriever regime, and hallucinated hypothetical speeches risk injecting wrong entities.

nodes.label: When do expansions fail?
nodes.summary: Across 11 expansion techniques x 24 retrievers x 12 datasets: strong negative correlation between retriever strength and expansion gains; expansion generally harms strong models.
nodes.relevance: Central citation predicting HyDE/multi-query would hurt nDCG for ParliamentRAG's strong gated dense channel while possibly helping recall.

nodes.label: monoT5 reranking
nodes.summary: T5 generates true/false as relevance; strong zero-shot cross-domain reranking, robust in low-data and legal settings.
nodes.relevance: The practical cross-encoder family (multilingual descendants like bge-reranker-v2-m3) for the reranker ablation arm.

nodes.label: RankGPT
nodes.summary: Listwise permutation-generation reranking with GPT-3.5/4 beats fine-tuned cross-encoders zero-shot; permutation distillation into a 440M model outperforms a 3B supervised model.
nodes.relevance: Upper-bound reranking arm at cost incompatible with SSE streaming; distillation argues the deployable option is a small cross-encoder.

nodes.label: GraphRAG (Microsoft)
nodes.summary: LLM-extracted entity graph + community summaries for global sensemaking queries; evaluation is LLM-judge head-to-head with no standard IR metrics.
nodes.relevance: Most-cited graph-RAG reference but weak evidence; ParliamentRAG's graph is curated institutional structure, sidestepping extraction noise.

nodes.label: HippoRAG
nodes.summary: OpenIE-built KG + Personalized PageRank seeded by query entities for single-step multi-hop retrieval; up to 20% better on multi-hop QA at 10-20x lower cost.
nodes.relevance: The peer-reviewed precedent for 'graph channel adds what dense misses'; PPR is a soft upgrade path for ParliamentRAG's hard 2-hop traversal.

nodes.label: BM25 strong in legal retrieval
nodes.summary: Vanilla BM25 placed 2nd in COLIEE 2021 case retrieval, above nearly all neural submissions; the broader pattern holds across legal corpora.
nodes.relevance: Strongest domain-transfer prior that a BM25 arm will show gains on terminology-heavy parliamentary text.

nodes.label: LegalBench-RAG
nodes.summary: 6,858 QA pairs over 700+ contracts with precise citation-span annotations, built to evaluate the retrieval component of legal RAG separately from generation.
nodes.relevance: Methodological template for the missing ParliamentRAG retrieval test collection: span-level relevance decoupled from generation.

nodes.label: Don't Stop Pretraining (DAPT)
nodes.summary: Domain-adaptive and task-adaptive continued pretraining yield consistent classification gains across 4 domains and 8 tasks; gains largest for distant domains.
nodes.relevance: Canonical justification for a Camera-DAPT encoder, with the caveat that all its evidence is classification, not retrieval.

nodes.label: CaseHOLD (When does pretraining help?)
nodes.summary: Legal DAPT gains appear only on difficult, highly domain-specific tasks (+7.2 F1 on CaseHOLD); gains scale with task difficulty times domain specificity.
nodes.relevance: Predicts parliamentary DAPT pays off only if the eval stresses parliamentary-specific semantics: motivates hard register-specific queries in the qrels.

nodes.label: LEGAL-BERT
nodes.summary: Legal-domain BERT variants beat vanilla BERT on domain tasks, but gains are modest and dataset-dependent; scratch vs continued pretraining mostly comparable.
nodes.relevance: Template and tempering evidence for a domain-encoder release; classification/NER only, no retrieval.

nodes.label: ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT
nodes.summary: Continued pretraining of Italian BERT on Italian civil-law corpora, evaluated on Italian legal downstream tasks.
nodes.relevance: Proof the Italian ecosystem produces domain BERTs for the closest adjacent register; nobody has done the parliamentary equivalent, which the ablation would be first to do.

nodes.label: PoliBERTweet
nodes.summary: BERTweet continued-pretrained on 83M US-election tweets; outperforms general LMs on political downstream tasks including stance detection.
nodes.relevance: The main political-domain encoder in the literature: same evidence pattern as XLM-R-Parla, same retrieval gap.

nodes.label: ParlBERT-German / FrameASt
nodes.summary: GermanBERT continued-pretrained on German parliamentary debates (v2 on >30M political sentences from GerParCor); used for CAP topic classification.
nodes.relevance: Closest German analogue of the proposed Camera-DAPT arm; again evaluated only on classification, never retrieval.

nodes.label: ParlaSent multilingual / XLM-R-Parla
nodes.summary: Introduces XLM-R-Parla (XLM-R-large DAPT on 1.72B words of 26-30 European parliaments incl. Italian) and the multilingual ParlaSent sentiment dataset; DAPT significantly improves downstream sentiment, rivaling GPT-4o zero-shot.
nodes.relevance: Strongest peer-reviewed parliamentary-DAPT model and the natural base for the DAPT ablation arm; never evaluated as an embedding/retrieval model.

nodes.label: Anisotropy of contextual embeddings
nodes.summary: All layers of BERT/ELMo/GPT-2 produce highly anisotropic representations confined to a narrow cone, worst in top layers.
nodes.relevance: Root of the argument that MLM-trained encoders do not give usable similarity spaces by mean-pooling.

nodes.label: SimCSE
nodes.summary: Unsupervised (dropout positives) and supervised (NLI) contrastive sentence embeddings; large STS gains; contrastive objective regularizes the anisotropic space.
nodes.relevance: The minimal contrastive head to bolt onto XLM-R-Parla or a Camera-DAPT encoder; STS gains do not equal retrieval gains.

nodes.label: TSDAE
nodes.summary: Denoising-autoencoder sentence-embedding pretraining beats prior unsupervised methods and is explicitly shown to significantly outperform MLM as a domain-adaptation step for embeddings.
nodes.relevance: Direct published evidence that MLM is the wrong adaptation objective for embeddings, the exact reason Knesset-DictaBERT-style DAPT is predicted not to help retrieval alone.

nodes.label: GPL (Generative Pseudo Labeling)
nodes.summary: Unsupervised domain adaptation of dense retrieval: synthetic queries + hard negatives + cross-encoder pseudo-labels + MarginMSE; up to +9.3 nDCG@10 on specialized BEIR domains, +1.4 more with TSDAE init.
nodes.relevance: THE method for the label-free Camera adaptation arm; its numbers are English-only, so an Italian parliamentary GPL result would be first.

nodes.label: InPars
nodes.summary: GPT-3 few-shot prompting generates synthetic (query, doc) pairs; rerankers trained on them gain 7-30% over BM25.
nodes.relevance: LLM-generated queries serve double duty: training pairs and the qrels bootstrap for the evaluation query set.

nodes.label: Promptagator
nodes.summary: Few-shot dense retrieval from 8 examples: LLM as task-specific query generator with consistency filtering trains dual encoders beating ColBERTv2 on BEIR.
nodes.relevance: Refines the adaptation arm: query generation should mimic ParliamentRAG's actual intent distribution, seeded from the existing 15-topic benchmark.

nodes.label: AdaSent
nodes.summary: A sentence-embedding adapter trained once on the base PLM can be inserted into any DAPT-ed variant, decoupling domain knowledge from sentence-embedding ability.
nodes.relevance: Cleanest articulation that DAPT and embedding ability are separable, composable ingredients: the conceptual frame for the XLM-R-Parla + contrastive-head arm.

nodes.label: ChipNeMo
nodes.summary: Industrial report: fine-tuning a small retriever with only 3,000 auto-generated domain samples improved retriever hit rate by ~30%, a better cost/benefit than full-model DAPT.
nodes.relevance: Order-of-magnitude datapoint that thousands of synthetic pairs suffice for large domain-retrieval gains at Camera-corpus scale.

nodes.label: MMTEB
nodes.summary: Massive multilingual embedding benchmark (500+ tasks, incl. MTEB(Europe) with Italian): multilingual-e5-large-instruct (560M) is the best public model overall; no parliamentary/political retrieval task exists in any language.
nodes.relevance: Defines the strong open baseline the DAPT arms must beat, and confirms the parliamentary-retrieval-task gap.

nodes.label: Wordscores
nodes.summary: Supervised text scaling: transfer word scores from reference texts with known (expert-survey) positions to virgin texts.
nodes.relevance: Canonical precedent that text-derived positions are validated against expert surveys; source of the reference-anchor idea ParliamentRAG has disabled in config.

nodes.label: Wordfish
nodes.summary: Unsupervised Poisson scaling of word frequencies onto one latent dimension; the recovered dimension is whatever dominates word-use variation, not necessarily left-right.
nodes.relevance: The natural non-LLM baseline for the compass; its documented failure on parliamentary speech (recovering institutional dimensions) is the confound the compass must be tested against.

nodes.label: Wordshoal
nodes.summary: Two-stage legislative-speech scaling (per-debate Wordfish + cross-debate factor analysis); in the Irish Dail the dominant dimension is government vs opposition, not left-right.
nodes.relevance: Closest classic analogue to per-query positioning, and the source of ParliamentRAG's main artifact risk: majority-vs-opposition clustering regardless of axis semantics.

nodes.label: Position taking in EP speeches
nodes.summary: Scaling European Parliament speeches recovers EU-integration and national divisions rather than left-right, even though left-right organizes EP voting.
nodes.relevance: Speech-derived positions can substantively diverge from vote/manifesto positions, so imperfect CHES correlation is partly informative, not only error.

nodes.label: Speeches vs votes (Swiss parliament)
nodes.summary: Speech-based ideal points correlate with vote-based ones but show greater intra-party spread; voting is discipline-constrained, speech less so.
nodes.relevance: The standard justification for a speech-based compass, and motivation for a roll-call convergent-validity check using the 6.9M-vote graph.

nodes.label: Scaling coded texts (Lowe et al.)
nodes.summary: Log odds-ratio scaling of manifesto category counts, validated against expert surveys; demonstrates construction of issue-specific scales beyond one left-right axis.
nodes.relevance: The theoretical warrant for per-query issue-specific axes, with the warning that aggregate and issue scales can disagree.

nodes.label: Validating Wordscores
nodes.summary: Systematic validity framework for text scaling: content validity (which words drive scores), criterion validity (expert-survey correlation), construct validity (predicting known memberships).
nodes.relevance: Provides the three-part validity checklist the compass validation replicates.

nodes.label: Computers, coders, and voters
nodes.summary: Inter-method validation over 254 manifestos: Wordscores agrees with CMP/experts/voters in Germany and Denmark, Wordfish only in Germany; method validity is corpus-contingent.
nodes.relevance: Template for quadrangulation and justification for an Italian-corpus-specific validation rather than citing foreign successes.

nodes.label: Text as Data (validate, validate, validate)
nodes.summary: The field's governing doctrine: automated text measures have no default validity; every application must demonstrate the measure captures the claimed concept.
nodes.relevance: The citation framing the entire compass-validation section of any ParliamentRAG paper.

nodes.label: Human judgment as benchmark
nodes.summary: Validates text-scaling output against aggregated human judgments of the same texts when no external gold standard exists at the right granularity.
nodes.relevance: The precedent for validating fragment-level stance scores, which no expert survey covers.

nodes.label: Crowd-sourced text analysis
nodes.summary: Aggregated non-expert crowd codings of manifesto sentences reproduce expert codings; reproducibility as a validity criterion.
nodes.relevance: Design template for a low-cost human validation arm rating Italian fragment stances.

nodes.label: Party embeddings
nodes.summary: Doc2vec-style training with party-session indicator vectors over UK/Canada/US parliamentary corpora; principal components of party vectors recover validated left-right placements (validated against CMP, expert surveys, roll calls).
nodes.relevance: Strongest published precedent that embedding geometry over parliamentary speech carries ideological signal; the method ParliaBench's PSA adapts and the corpus-level baseline for the compass.

nodes.label: Cross-lingual embedding scaling
nodes.summary: Word-frequency scaling barely correlates with actual left-right placements while semantically-informed embedding scaling predicts positions better, with no cross-lingual drop.
nodes.relevance: Early evidence for 'projection tracks vocabulary, not stance': why the compass moved from embedding projection to LLM stance scoring.

nodes.label: Linear political representations in LLMs
nodes.summary: Linear probes on LLM activations predict US lawmakers' DW-NOMINATE scores at Spearman ~0.8; steering along the probe direction shifts generated slant.
nodes.relevance: Mechanistic support that ideology-as-direction is real inside LLMs; indirect backing for axis-vector construction.

nodes.label: LLM pairwise scaling of politicians
nodes.summary: LLM pairwise comparisons of senators aggregated with Bradley-Terry produce liberal-conservative and issue-specific scales correlating strongly with roll-call measures.
nodes.relevance: Closest methodological cousin to per-query axes; pairwise elicitation is a robustness alternative to direct scalar stance scoring.

nodes.label: Measurement in the age of LLMs
nodes.summary: Elicits numeric ideology scores for legislators and texts directly from LLMs; scores accord with established scaling; frames LLMs as measurement instruments requiring criterion validation.
nodes.relevance: Direct precedent for numeric LLM stance scoring and its validation framing.

nodes.label: Positioning by asking and averaging
nodes.summary: Ask an LLM where a text stands on a focal dimension and average many responses: correlations with expert/crowd/roll-call benchmarks exceed .90 for best models, across 10 languages.
nodes.relevance: Sets the achievable agreement ceiling and gives 'averaging many small judgments' (the compass's mean-over-fragments) a citable pedigree.

nodes.label: Mapping (A)Ideology (LLM vs CHES)
nodes.summary: GPT-3.5 pairwise party comparisons (names only, no text) aggregated with Bradley-Terry closely reproduce CHES orderings for European parties including Italy.
nodes.relevance: Introduces the crucial caveat: the LLM already knows party reputations, so the compass must prove it tracks retrieved evidence, not the model's prior (label-masking test).

nodes.label: ChatGPT vs expert survey (France)
nodes.summary: ChatGPT and local experts placed French parties on CHES items simultaneously: LLM close to experts on salient dimensions (left-right, EU, immigration), weaker on fringe issues and party characteristics.
nodes.relevance: The exact template for per-issue validation, and the basis for pre-registering heterogeneous agreement expectations.

nodes.label: LLM NLU-based scaling (AJPS)
nodes.summary: Argues for holistic 'read then score' LLM analysis of political texts against classify-and-count, benchmarked on crowd/expert data; the Wordscores authors migrating to LLM-NLU.
nodes.relevance: Supports the compass's stage separation (analyze then score) and whole-fragment stance reading, with an AJPS imprimatur.

nodes.label: Political Compass or Spinning Arrow?
nodes.summary: LLM political-compass results are unstable under paraphrase and format changes; constrained questionnaires do not reflect real usage.
nodes.relevance: Mandates prompt-perturbation robustness checks for axis generation and stance prompts; the rebuttal is that ParliamentRAG scores parliamentary evidence, not model opinions, which must be shown empirically.

nodes.label: ChatGPT outperforms crowd workers
nodes.summary: Zero-shot ChatGPT beats MTurk crowds on relevance/stance/topic/frame annotation of political text with higher intercoder agreement.
nodes.relevance: Baseline legitimacy of LLM stance annotation, though it measures agreement with researcher labels, not political neutrality.

nodes.label: GPT-4 political annotation (Tornberg)
nodes.summary: GPT-4 beats experts and crowds at inferring party affiliation from tweets with equal or lower bias, introducing a party-asymmetric error metric.
nodes.relevance: The party-asymmetric accuracy metric is exactly the right bias diagnostic for the compass's stance scorer.

nodes.label: LLMs as substitute annotators
nodes.summary: GPT-4 political text annotation approaches expert quality across tasks and languages; recommends keeping a human-coded validation subset.
nodes.relevance: Bounds how much to trust the LLM stance layer and motivates per-party human agreement checks.

nodes.label: Political bias in LLM stance classification
nodes.summary: 7 LLMs x 3 datasets: statistically significant stance-classification performance differences by political orientation of the target; telling the model about the bias does not fix it.
nodes.relevance: Very high-risk citation: the stance scorer may be differentially accurate across Italian parties, mandating per-party error analysis.

nodes.label: Sentiment is not stance
nodes.summary: Sentiment classifiers systematically mismeasure stance (angry yet supportive speech); stance must be target-aware.
nodes.relevance: Justifies the compass's explicit rebuttal handling and the coherence validator's separation of sentiment from stance mismatch.

nodes.label: Preprocessing sensitivity
nodes.summary: Unsupervised text-analysis results, including scaling, can flip under defensible alternative preprocessing; sensitivity should be reported.
nodes.relevance: The analogue for the compass: report sensitivity across fragment-clip length, batch composition, and axis-description wording.

nodes.label: Evaluating expert judgments
nodes.summary: Psychometric toolkit for expert surveys: inter-expert reliability, expert-level bias, convergence with independent measures.
nodes.relevance: When the compass disagrees with CHES on a party, check CHES's own expert dissent first; disagreement on high-dissent items is uninformative.

nodes.label: Cross-validating party positioning
nodes.summary: Compares expert survey vs manifesto vs voter survey vs elite survey on the same construct; expert surveys emerge as most accurate; founding paper of the triangulation doctrine.
nodes.relevance: Direct methodological template for the multi-source compass validation table (CHES, ParlGov, POPPA).

nodes.label: GAL-TAN (Hooghe, Marks & Wilson)
nodes.summary: Origin of the GAL-TAN second dimension: economic left-right and cultural liberal-authoritarian are distinct, partially orthogonal axes.
nodes.relevance: Theoretical grounding for a two-axis compass rather than a single left-right, though ParliamentRAG's axes are query-local.

nodes.label: Political preferences of LLMs
nodes.summary: 11 political-orientation instruments administered to 24 conversational LLMs: most RLHF'd chat models diagnosed left-of-center; modest fine-tuning steers orientation.
nodes.relevance: Establishes the prior that the GPT-4.1 generator likely carries a directional lean independent of the corpus, so retrieval balance is necessary but not sufficient.

nodes.label: Measuring ChatGPT political bias
nodes.summary: Impersonation-vs-default differencing with randomization and placebo tests finds systematic partisan lean (US, Brazil, UK).
nodes.relevance: The differencing design transfers: a neutral answer should be roughly equidistant from per-party-conditioned generations.

nodes.label: Whose opinions do LMs reflect? (OpinionQA)
nodes.summary: Aligns LM answer distributions with Pew survey distributions for 60 US demographic groups; substantial misalignment; RLHF shifts models toward left-leaning demographics.
nodes.relevance: Canonical method for distributional opinion alignment against external ground truth: the model to imitate for validating outputs against Italian survey/CHES data.

nodes.label: What is said and how it is said
nodes.summary: Decomposes political bias into content (stance substance) and style (framing/polarity); models can hold the same position while framing it asymmetrically.
nodes.relevance: Directly transfers to answer auditing: equal quotation with unequal framing is a failure mode retrieval metrics cannot see.

nodes.label: Hidden Persuaders
nodes.summary: 18 LLMs show candidate preference in voting simulations; interaction with an LLM measurably shifted likely voters' views.
nodes.relevance: The stakes argument: an unbalanced parliamentary QA system is potentially opinion-shifting, justifying fairness as a first-class evaluation objective.

nodes.label: FA*IR fair top-k ranking
nodes.summary: Ranked group fairness: every top-k prefix must contain a minimum fraction of protected-group items, tested against a binomial model; utility maximized subject to the constraint.
nodes.relevance: The direct formal ancestor of the min-5-per-party quota, and the upgrade path to statistically derived per-party floors.

nodes.label: Fairness of Exposure in Rankings
nodes.summary: Rank position allocates exposure; proposes optimizing rankings under exposure constraints, notably group exposure proportional to group merit (average relevance).
nodes.relevance: The literature precedent for conditioning treatment on relevance, not raw share: 'exposure proportional to merit' is the null hypothesis ParliamentRAG should test.

nodes.label: Equity of Attention
nodes.summary: Attention should be proportional to relevance amortized over a sequence of rankings, since a single ranking cannot be fair.
nodes.relevance: Justifies reporting fairness aggregated over query sets rather than per query: per-query balance can be impossible for one-party motions.

nodes.label: Expected Exposure (Diaz et al.)
nodes.summary: Defines target exposure under an ideal randomizing policy and measures deviation, decomposable into disparity and relevance components.
nodes.relevance: Gives a principled scalar separating 'unfair' from 'just less relevant' for per-party exposure in the merged pool and answers.

nodes.label: Fairness in Ranking survey
nodes.summary: Two-part ACM Computing Surveys taxonomy of fair-ranking formalizations and the normative assumptions each metric encodes.
nodes.relevance: The citation for framing ParliamentRAG's mix of in-processing score adjustments and post-processing prefix quota, and for stating its normative worldview.

nodes.label: Should I Follow the Crowd?
nodes.summary: Probabilistic separation of item popularity from true relevance; popularity-rewarding offline metrics can invert true effectiveness.
nodes.relevance: Cleanest conceptual precedent for 'corpus share is not relevance': FdI/PD dominate chunks the way popular items dominate ratings; motivates counterfactual reweighting.

nodes.label: Popularity bias survey
nodes.summary: Catalogues popularity-bias metrics (popularity lift, Gini over exposure, recommendation-vs-popularity correlation) and mitigation families, plus feedback-loop amplification evidence.
nodes.relevance: The output-share-on-input-popularity regression proposed as ParliamentRAG's headline fairness test is standard practice in this literature.

nodes.label: Controlling popularity bias in LtR
nodes.summary: Adds a popularity-dispersion regularizer to learning-to-rank to balance head vs tail item exposure.
nodes.relevance: Shows the merger's coverage term (penalizing over-represented parties) is a known in-processing debiasing pattern, not an ad-hoc hack.

nodes.label: Does RAG introduce unfairness?
nodes.summary: Scenario-based fairness evaluation of RAG: fairness issues persist in both retrieval and generation stages even when utility improves; multi-stage architectures make mitigation hard.
nodes.relevance: Supports auditing ParliamentRAG stage by stage (channels, merger, expert selection, writer, surgeon), since each has a different party-bias mechanism.

nodes.label: No Free Lunch (RAG undermines fairness)
nodes.summary: RAG can undo fairness alignment without fine-tuning; even fully censored external corpora still yield biased outputs: the retrieval mechanism itself introduces bias.
nodes.relevance: Sharpest counter to 'official parliamentary record, therefore neutral': measured balance metrics, not corpus provenance, are the answer.

nodes.label: Towards FairRAG (exposure at retrieval time)
nodes.summary: On TREC Fair Ranking data, representative stochastic rankers achieve near-parity exposure, and generation demographic parity closely mirrors exposure parity.
nodes.relevance: Empirical support for enforcing balance at the merger (retrieval time) rather than prompt-begging the writer; preprint, supporting not load-bearing.

nodes.label: When Not to Trust Language Models (PopQA)
nodes.summary: LM factual recall tracks entity popularity; retrieval augmentation helps precisely on unpopular entities.
nodes.relevance: The generator's parametric prior about Italian parties is popularity-skewed, so even perfect retrieval balance faces a skewed prior at writing time.

nodes.label: What Drives Media Slant?
nodes.summary: Text-based slant index: outlet language similarity to congressional partisan phrase distributions, then regression-decomposed onto demand and supply factors.
nodes.relevance: Method transfer (centroid/phrase-based slant of generated answers against per-party speech distributions) and the regression-decomposition template for share-on-share calibration.

nodes.label: Fair and Balanced? (crowdsourced media bias)
nodes.summary: 749 judges classify 10,950 articles: bias manifests mostly as issue selection and lopsided negative coverage of the out-group, not overt advocacy.
nodes.relevance: Warns fairness is not only how much each party appears but in what light: motivates the quote-valence lopsidedness statistic per party.

nodes.label: Pretraining term frequencies
nodes.summary: Few-shot accuracy strongly correlates with pretraining term frequency (up to ~70-point gaps between frequency deciles).
nodes.relevance: The general mechanism behind party-size bias at generation time: the model is simply better at frequent entities, predicting quality disparities for small groups.

nodes.label: Long-tail knowledge (Kandpal et al.)
nodes.summary: QA accuracy scales with the count of relevant pretraining documents; retrieval augmentation is the effective long-tail mitigation.
nodes.relevance: Completes the frequency triad: frequency drives behavior, retrieval fixes the tail; ParliamentRAG's grounding+quota design is the prescribed mitigation.

nodes.label: Perspective-varied political summarization
nodes.summary: Benchmark for independently summarizing each political perspective in opinionated documents; all 11 tested models struggle to stay faithful to the intended perspective.
nodes.relevance: Evidence that per-party perspective-conditioned summarization is hard, and a source of evaluation dimensions for perspective faithfulness.

nodes.label: MODS (moderated multi-perspective summarization)
nodes.summary: Panel architecture of per-document speaker LLMs plus a moderator with a topic plan: 38-59% gains in topic coverage and perspective balance, with citation-based balance metrics.
nodes.relevance: Closest architectural cousin to per-party expert selection + staged generation; a candidate baseline with directly comparable balance numbers.

nodes.label: ParlaMint 5.0
nodes.summary: 29 uniformly TEI-encoded European parliamentary corpora (8.07M speeches, 1.23B words, >20 languages, mostly 2015-2022) with speaker/party/role metadata, a mandatory chair/regular/guest speaker taxonomy, and v5.0 CAP topic labels; CC BY 4.0 on CLARIN.SI.
nodes.relevance: The field's reference schema ParliamentRAG's Neo4j model should align with; its speaker-type taxonomy is the citable standard for procedural filtering.

nodes.label: ParlaMint-IT (Senato)
nodes.summary: Italian ParlaMint component: Senato della Repubblica only, ~2013 to ~mid-2022 (legislatures XVII-XVIII), ~79k speeches, ~31M words, TEI + UD annotation.
nodes.relevance: Different chamber and essentially disjoint time window from Camera XIX: usable only for cross-chamber transfer and distribution checks, not as gold overlap.

nodes.label: ItaParlCorpus
nodes.summary: Italian Camera dei Deputati speeches 1948-2022 (legislatures I-XVIII): ~2.4M speeches, 470M words, 5,830 speakers, 77 parties, CC BY 4.0 on Harvard Dataverse.
nodes.relevance: Ends exactly where ParliamentRAG's corpus begins; the natural DAPT pretraining corpus for an Italian parliamentary encoder and a historical validation substrate.

nodes.label: Knesset Corpus
nodes.summary: All Israeli plenary and committee protocols of ~3 decades: >30M sentences, >384M tokens, morpho-syntactic and NER annotation, speaker metadata; CC BY 4.0.
nodes.relevance: The DAPT substrate of Knesset-DictaBERT; committee protocols are a coverage dimension ParliamentRAG currently lacks.

nodes.label: Hansard Corpus (UK)
nodes.summary: British Parliament 1803-2005: 7.6M speeches, 1.6B words, semantically tagged (SAMUELS).
nodes.relevance: Scale reference for diachronic parliamentary retrieval and UK transfer experiments.

nodes.label: Open Discourse (Bundestag)
nodes.summary: German Bundestag plenary protocols 1949-2022: ~900k speeches, >4,200 speakers, 2.5M interjection records in relational tables.
nodes.relevance: The German comparative corpus; a template (and cautionary tale on speaker-attribution parsing errors) for corpus releases.

nodes.label: GerParCor
nodes.summary: German-language parliamentary protocols from DE/AT/CH/LI across three centuries, OCR'd and spaCy-annotated.
nodes.relevance: Training substrate of ParlBERT-v2; shows the corpus scale available for parliamentary DAPT in a well-resourced language.

nodes.label: ParlVote / ParlVote+
nodes.summary: 34,010 UK Commons debate speeches labeled with the speaker's subsequent vote on the debated motion; ParlVote+ adds manual policy-preference labels.
nodes.relevance: The design template for building an Italian vote-linked stance dataset from ParliamentRAG's 17.3k roll calls plus speech graph, which no one has done.

nodes.label: ConVote
nodes.summary: 3,857 US House floor-debate speech segments (2005) annotated with speaker, party, bill, and vote (support/oppose).
nodes.relevance: Foundational vote-supervised stance corpus; cross-lingual pretraining material for an Italian analogue.

nodes.label: ParlaSent 1.0
nodes.summary: 18,200 sentiment-annotated parliamentary sentences (BCS, CZ, SK, SL, EN-UK) with the 6-level reduction-friendly schema; no Italian data.
nodes.relevance: Companion dataset of XLM-R-ParlaSent; zero-shot transfer to Italian is plausible but unmeasured, a gap ParliamentRAG could close with a small gold sample.

nodes.label: ParlaCAP dataset
nodes.summary: ~8M ParlaMint 5.0 speeches across 28 parliaments silver-labeled with 22 CAP major topics plus sentiment and PartyFacts/V-Dem IDs; CC BY 4.0; Italian slice is Senate-only with unmeasured accuracy.
nodes.relevance: A ready topic layer and distributional sanity check for Camera XIX; genuine Italian validation requires new gold annotation.

nodes.label: Touche Ideology & Power (CLEF)
nodes.summary: Shared-task datasets from ParlaMint 4.0 with per-speech binary left/right ideology and coalition/opposition power labels.
nodes.relevance: The reference resource for ideology/power classification baselines relevant to the compass and to the government-vs-opposition confound.

nodes.label: ParlSpeech V2
nodes.summary: 6.3M speeches from 9 chambers (no Italy), 21-32 years each, with speaker/party/agenda metadata and chair markers.
nodes.relevance: The comparative-politics workhorse whose chair-flag convention supports procedural filtering; also a generalization target.

nodes.label: IMPAQTS / IMPAQTS-PID
nodes.summary: Italian multimodal political-speech corpus (1946-2023) with expert pragmatic annotation of implicit content; PID subset has 31,822 passages with validated implicature explanations.
nodes.relevance: The only Italian political corpus with pragmatic gold: an adversarial probe for stance scoring and citation-coherence robustness to implicit content.

nodes.label: ParlEE (incl. Italy)
nodes.summary: Sentence-level plenary speeches with CAP policy-area annotation, 2009-2019; V3 includes Italy among six chambers.
nodes.relevance: The only other pre-existing (silver) CAP-annotated Italian parliamentary resource at sentence level; ends 2019.

nodes.label: EuroCon
nodes.summary: 2,225 European Parliament deliberation records (2009-2022) as issue/stances/resolution/votes sextuples for LLM consensus-finding evaluation.
nodes.relevance: Sister parliamentary benchmark and a rare votes+stances-linked EP resource; maps the benchmark landscape ParliamentRAG sits in.

nodes.label: HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic
nodes.summary: 1,782 multi-hop questions over French Third Republic parliamentary debates and newspapers (1870-1940), requiring cross-source synthesis and temporal reasoning.
nodes.relevance: The closest existing thing to a parliamentary QA benchmark: historical and French, so the contemporary-parliament gap remains.

nodes.label: Multi-EuP
nodes.summary: 22K European Parliament documents in 24 official EU languages with cross-lingual relevance judgments and speaker demographics, built for studying language/demographic bias in ranking.
nodes.relevance: The closest existing parliamentary IR dataset, but bias-focused and EP-register; a possible external validation set for adapted retrievers.

nodes.label: MTEB
nodes.summary: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: 8 task types, 58 datasets, 112 languages; no universal winner; original Italian retrieval coverage effectively absent.
nodes.relevance: The embedder-selection reference whose parliamentary/political blind spot motivates building ParliamentRAG's own qrels.

nodes.label: PartyFacts
nodes.summary: Stable cross-dataset party identifiers with crosswalks to ParlGov, MARPOR, CHES, and ParlSpeech.
nodes.relevance: Adopting PartyFacts IDs for the 10 Camera groups makes every external validation join reproducible.

nodes.label: CHES 2024
nodes.summary: Chapel Hill Expert Survey 2024: 279 parties, 31 countries, fielded late 2024, 0-10 scales on ~55 variables (lrgen/lrecon/galtan plus ~20 issue positions, salience, dissent, blur); covers 10 Italian parties incl. FdI, PD, M5S, Lega, FI; Italia Viva and Noi Moderati absent; free CSV.
