nodes.relevance: The primary, temporally matched external ground truth for validating the ideological compass at the issue level.

nodes.label: Manifesto Project (MARPOR/RILE)
nodes.summary: Expert-coded party manifestos with RILE left-right scores; verified negative: the Italian 2022 election is absent from releases 2023a-2025a, so no RILE for XIX-legislature manifestos.
nodes.relevance: Cannot anchor the Italian compass for this legislature; CHES 2024 is the only matched expert source, which itself must be stated as a limitation.

nodes.label: ParlGov 2024
nodes.summary: Parties, elections, cabinets for EU/OECD democracies with composite left-right placements and cabinet composition; covers essentially all Italian parliamentary parties including small ones.
nodes.relevance: Coarse but complete fallback for parties CHES misses (e.g. Noi Moderati) and the ground truth for the maggioranza/opposizione coalition logic.

nodes.label: POPPA 2023
nodes.summary: Populism and Political Parties Expert Survey: 312 parties, 31 countries (2023), Italy included; specialist instrument for populism/anti-elite dimensions.
nodes.relevance: Supplementary criterion for anti-elitism-like compass axes (casta, vitalizi, direct democracy) that CHES covers only thinly.

nodes.label: BM25
nodes.summary: Probabilistic lexical ranking with saturating term frequency and length normalization; robust zero-shot baseline that often beats dense models out of domain.
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG has a Lucene full-text index provisioned but no sparse channel; act numbers, names, and EuroVoc terms are BM25's best case.

nodes.label: Dense passage retrieval (bi-encoder)
nodes.summary: Dual-encoder dense retrieval trained contrastively; the architecture behind ParliamentRAG's dense channel.
nodes.relevance: Strong on topical matching, documented to fail on rare entities: the reason for the graph channel and the hybrid ablation.

nodes.label: HyDE
nodes.summary: Retrieve with the embedding of an LLM-generated hypothetical answer document instead of the query.
nodes.relevance: PolicyBot-style default whose literature prior for a strong in-domain retriever is negative: a planned ablation arm and likely negative result.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
nodes.summary: Rank-based fusion: sum of 1/(k+rank) over input rankings, k=60; scale-free and parameter-light.
nodes.relevance: The standard fusion ParliamentRAG's convex merger must be compared against; cannot express coverage/diversity objectives.

nodes.label: Cross-encoder reranking
nodes.summary: Joint query-document scoring with a transformer after first-stage retrieval; best zero-shot effectiveness in BEIR at high inference cost.
nodes.relevance: The reranker ablation arm, to be placed upstream of the merger so it does not fight the party quota.

nodes.label: MMR / xQuAD diversification
nodes.summary: Greedy relevance-vs-redundancy trade-off (MMR) and explicit aspect-coverage diversification (xQuAD).
nodes.relevance: The direct lineage of ParliamentRAG's diversity/coverage terms and per-party quota: explicit diversification over exogenous party aspects.

nodes.label: Hybrid dense+sparse retrieval
nodes.summary: Interpolation or fusion of lexical and dense channels; consistently beats either alone once the sparse baseline is properly tuned.
nodes.relevance: The highest-prior missing piece of the multi-view retriever for entity-heavy parliamentary queries.

nodes.label: text-embedding-3-small
nodes.summary: OpenAI's closed 1536-d embedder used by ParliamentRAG for everything; documented only by a vendor blog (MIRACL 44.0 avg, MTEB-EN 62.3); no Italian evaluation exists anywhere.
nodes.relevance: The incumbent whose Italian parliamentary competence is empirically unknown: the control arm of the embedding ablation.

nodes.label: Open multilingual embedders (BGE-M3, mE5)
nodes.summary: BGE-M3 (100+ languages, dense+sparse+multi-vector, 8k context; Findings of ACL 2024) and multilingual-e5-large-instruct (MMTEB's best public model).
nodes.relevance: The strong open baseline arm: parity would remove the proprietary dependency and set the bar DAPT arms must clear.

nodes.label: XLM-R-Parla (parliamentary DAPT encoder)
nodes.summary: XLM-R-large continued-pretrained on 1.72B words of European parliamentary text (incl. Italian); best open parliamentary checkpoint; MLM-only, so not an embedder out of the box.
nodes.relevance: The backbone of the parliamentary-DAPT ablation arm, requiring a contrastive head before it can serve retrieval.

nodes.label: Domain-adaptive pretraining (DAPT)
nodes.summary: Continued self-supervised pretraining on in-domain text; proven for classification, unproven for retrieval in the parliamentary domain.
nodes.relevance: The Knesset-DictaBERT recipe ParliamentRAG would replicate for Italian, with the retrieval evaluation everyone else omitted.

nodes.label: SimCSE / TSDAE contrastive heads
nodes.summary: Unsupervised contrastive (dropout-positive) and denoising-autoencoder objectives that turn MLM encoders into usable sentence embedders.
nodes.relevance: The mandatory embedding-head step between any parliamentary DAPT encoder and the dense channel.

nodes.label: GPL (generative pseudo labeling)
nodes.summary: Synthetic-query generation + hard-negative mining + cross-encoder pseudo-labels + MarginMSE to adapt a dense retriever to an unlabeled corpus.
nodes.relevance: The highest-expected-payoff adaptation method for the Camera corpus; an Italian parliamentary GPL result would be the first non-English one.

nodes.label: Wordfish scaling
nodes.summary: Unsupervised Poisson IRT scaling of word frequencies onto a latent dimension.
nodes.relevance: The non-LLM compass baseline whose known parliamentary failure mode (recovering government-vs-opposition) is the confound test.

nodes.label: Wordscores scaling
nodes.summary: Supervised scaling transferring word scores from reference texts with expert-known positions.
nodes.relevance: The anchor-based alternative: ParliamentRAG's disabled left/center/right anchors are a Wordscores-style device that validation could revive.

nodes.label: Party embeddings
nodes.summary: Doc2vec-style training with party-period indicator vectors; principal components recover validated left-right placements.
nodes.relevance: Corpus-level compass baseline over the 40k+ speeches, and the machinery behind ParliaBench's centroid metrics.

nodes.label: LLM political positioning
nodes.summary: Eliciting positions from LLMs by direct scoring, pairwise comparison + Bradley-Terry, or ask-and-average, validated against expert surveys at r>.90 for best models.
nodes.relevance: The method family the per-query compass belongs to; its validation designs (per-issue CHES comparison, label masking) define the compass protocol.

nodes.label: CAP topic classification
nodes.summary: 22-label Comparative Agendas Project major-topic classification of parliamentary speech, now available as a multilingual classifier covering Italian.
nodes.relevance: The ready-made topic layer for topic-aware authority scoring and per-topic fairness slices, comparable across 28 parliaments.

nodes.label: LLM teacher-student annotation
nodes.summary: GPT-4o annotates tens of thousands of instances (~$100), a fine-tuned encoder student matches the teacher at negligible inference cost; validated via human-LLM Krippendorff alpha.
nodes.relevance: The template for any ParliamentRAG component that must run over millions of passages instead of calling an LLM per query.

nodes.label: LLM-as-judge
nodes.summary: Using an LLM to score or compare system outputs; ~80% human agreement at best, with documented position, verbosity, self-preference, and family biases.
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG currently has no judge; if one is added it must be cross-family, both-order, kappa-calibrated, and PPI-anchored.

nodes.label: PoLL judge panel
nodes.summary: Panel of small judges from disjoint model families with vote/mean pooling; beats a single GPT-4 judge and mitigates intra-model bias at >7x lower cost.
nodes.relevance: The concrete judge design for evaluating GPT-4o outputs without family contamination.

nodes.label: Prediction-powered inference (PPI)
nodes.summary: Statistical estimators combining many cheap machine labels with a small human-labeled anchor set into unbiased estimates with honest confidence intervals.
nodes.relevance: Turns the existing 67 expert judgments into the calibration anchor for any automatic evaluator.

nodes.label: LLM relevance judgment (UMBRELA-style)
nodes.summary: LLM-assessed graded relevance labels over pooled results; modest per-label kappa but near-perfect system-ranking correlation; label as LLM-assisted, human-audited.
nodes.relevance: The only affordable route to the missing Italian parliamentary qrels, with a stratified expert audit.

nodes.label: TOST equivalence testing
nodes.summary: Two one-sided tests against a pre-registered smallest effect size of interest, converting 'not significant' into an affirmative equivalence/non-inferiority claim.
nodes.relevance: The tool for honestly claiming parity with NotebookLM and 'no party effect' in fairness audits.

nodes.label: Corpus-share calibration regression
nodes.summary: Regress per-party outcome shares on corpus shares (conditioning on per-party relevance mass): slope 1 = proportional pass-through, >1 = amplification, <1 = equalization; quality outcomes tested against slope 0.
nodes.relevance: The single most direct answer to 'does the system favor FdI/PD because they are big?', distinguishing amplification from the quota's intended equalization.

nodes.label: NLI entailment gating
nodes.summary: Sentence- or claim-level natural-language-inference checks of generated prose against retrieved evidence (SummaC/AlignScore/ALCE-style), multilingual via mDeBERTa-XNLI-class models.
nodes.relevance: The missing prose-verification layer that would complete the verbatim+entailment system.

nodes.label: Copy mechanisms / constrained decoding
nodes.summary: From soft pointer-generator copying to hard FM-index-constrained decoding (SEAL) that only emits corpus-attested substrings.
nodes.relevance: The generation-time alternatives to ParliamentRAG's post-hoc surgeon; SEAL-style decoding is its cited future path for local deployment.

nodes.label: nDCG@k / Recall@k
nodes.summary: Graded-relevance cumulated-gain ranking metrics (Jarvelin & Kekalainen 2002); the standard headline metrics for retrieval ablations.
nodes.relevance: The primary metrics for every qrels-based ParliamentRAG ablation (nDCG@10 headline, Recall@200 feeds the merger).

nodes.label: Citation precision/recall (ALCE)
nodes.summary: NLI-judged: recall = cited passages entail the statement; precision = leave-one-out relevance of each citation.
nodes.relevance: The layer Quote Fidelity does not cover; portable to Italian with a multilingual NLI model and stratifiable by party.

nodes.label: Quote Fidelity (QF)
nodes.summary: Fraction of quotes that are exact substrings of the source speech; 1.00 by construction in ParliamentRAG via the deterministic surgeon.
nodes.relevance: The system's hard invariant, to be framed as enforced QUIP=1.0 on quote spans, honestly scoped as quote authenticity, not prose entailment.

nodes.label: Groups with Quotation (GQ)
nodes.summary: Fraction of parliamentary groups represented with at least one verbatim quotation in an answer (0.97 vs baseline 0.95).
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG's coverage-recall metric with no published analogue; the per-party fairness headline number.

nodes.label: Krippendorff's alpha (and kappa)
nodes.summary: Chance-corrected inter-annotator agreement handling >=2 annotators, missing data, and ordinal scales; conventions: >=0.8 reliable, 0.667-0.8 tentative.
nodes.relevance: The IAA statistic for every human validation arm; ParliamentRAG's own alpha (-0.20 to 0.08) fails the tentative floor, motivating instrument redesign.

nodes.label: Cross-Context Stability = 100/(1+CV)
nodes.summary: ParliaBench's Eq. 4: 100/(1+CV) of a metric across context groups (parties/topics). Statistically fragile: requires ratio-scale positive data, explodes near zero means, has no null model, and conflates legitimate heterogeneity with unfairness.
nodes.relevance: Must be cited to ParliaBench (Koniaris et al., LREC 2026), never presented as original; usable only as a headline descriptive with bootstrap CIs and small-n correction.

nodes.label: Expected-exposure disparity
nodes.summary: Deviation of realized group exposure from relevance-proportional target exposure, decomposable into disparity and relevance components.
nodes.relevance: The merit-normalized replacement for raw dispersion in ParliamentRAG's party-fairness audit.

nodes.label: Gini over party exposure
nodes.summary: Inequality coefficient over group exposure shares, standard in popularity-bias work; bounded and decomposable.
nodes.relevance: Share-native complement to the calibration regression for the bias-propagation ledger C_p to R_p to E_p to S_p.

nodes.label: Political Spectrum Alignment (PSA)
nodes.summary: ParliaBench's two-stage centroid metric: cosine of a text to orientation centroids of real speeches, penalized by distance on a RILE-style -6..+6 axis.
nodes.relevance: A reusable compass-validation recipe whose weakness (corpus-internal ground truth, no CHES) is exactly what CHES anchoring improves on.

nodes.label: Party Alignment
nodes.summary: Cosine similarity of a text to the expected party's speech centroid; the full similarity vector over all parties is a per-answer balance probe.
nodes.relevance: Generalized to all parties, it becomes ParliamentRAG's centroid balance probe F8 for neutral answers.

nodes.label: QUIP-Score
nodes.summary: Character n-gram precision of output against a trusted corpus via Bloom-filter membership: verbatim grounding as exact string membership.
nodes.relevance: The metric-space analog of the surgeon; Quote Fidelity is QUIP=1.0 enforced on designated quote spans.

nodes.label: Procedural vs substantive speech
nodes.summary: Parliamentary turn counts are dominated by procedural output (chair: 55% of speeches, 5% of words in BasqueParl); chair/regular/guest is a mandatory ParlaMint taxonomy and procedural filtering is standard hygiene.
nodes.relevance: The main contamination threat to the interventions component and to dense retrieval candidacy.

nodes.label: Party-size bias
nodes.summary: The risk that a system over-serves parties dominating the corpus (FdI/PD hold the largest chunk shares), in retrieval share, exposure, citation share, or answer quality.
nodes.relevance: The central fairness threat model; ParliamentRAG's quota and coverage terms are its designed mitigations, so far unmeasured.

nodes.label: Popularity bias / long-tail effect
nodes.summary: Observed frequency conflates true relevance with exposure; LLM capability itself tracks entity frequency in pretraining data.
nodes.relevance: The general mechanism behind party-size bias at both retrieval and generation time; retrieval augmentation is the documented tail mitigation.

nodes.label: LLM prior leakage
nodes.summary: LLMs can reproduce CHES-like party placements from names alone, so an LLM-scored compass may measure the model's prior about parties rather than the retrieved evidence.
nodes.relevance: The single most important internal-validity threat to the compass; addressed by label-masking and label-shuffling tests.

nodes.label: Self/family-preference judge bias
nodes.summary: LLM judges favor their own and same-family outputs via style recognition and low-perplexity familiarity; contamination is harder to detect than position bias.
nodes.relevance: Why a GPT judge over GPT-4o answers is contaminated by construction, mandating cross-family panels.

nodes.label: Verbatim grounding / verifiability by design
nodes.summary: Making outputs quote exactly from a trusted corpus turns verification into an O(substring) check instead of probabilistic NLI.
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG's core design thesis, shared with QUIP/Quote-Tuning/SEAL, uniquely combined here with graph-inherited attribution.

nodes.label: Government-vs-opposition dimension
nodes.summary: In high-discipline parliaments the first latent dimension of speech is institutional role, not ideology (Wordshoal's Irish Dail finding).
nodes.relevance: The main artifact risk for the compass: majority parties may cluster against opposition regardless of the generated axis semantics; must be measured, not assumed away.

nodes.label: Citation correctness vs faithfulness
nodes.summary: A citation can be NLI-correct yet post-rationalized: the model never causally relied on it; up to ~57% of correct citations lack faithfulness.
nodes.relevance: Third axis for scoping ParliamentRAG's claims: verbatim quotes prove authenticity, entailment proves support, neither proves causal reliance.

nodes.label: MLM DAPT is not an embedder
nodes.summary: MLM-adapted encoders produce anisotropic, semantically poor pooled vectors; a contrastive/denoising head is required before retrieval use.
nodes.relevance: Predicts raw XLM-R-Parla will lose badly to generic embedders: the mandatory negative control of the embedding ablation.

nodes.label: Sentiment is not stance
nodes.summary: Tone and position are distinct: a speech can be angry and supportive; stance must be target-aware.
nodes.relevance: Grounds the compass's LLM stance scoring over sentiment/projection and the coherence validator's separate stance-mismatch check.

nodes.label: Expert finding
nodes.summary: Given a topic, rank people by expertise using documents and organizational evidence associated with them (TREC Enterprise lineage).
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG's per-party expert selection is an expert-finding task; its evaluation designs are the validation template.

nodes.label: Attributed / evidence-grounded QA
nodes.summary: Answer questions with explicit, verifiable pointers to supporting sources (AIS/ALCE lineage).
nodes.relevance: The task family ParliamentRAG instantiates for parliamentary records, with quotes as the attribution unit.

nodes.label: Political text scaling / ideology estimation
nodes.summary: Place actors or texts on latent ideological dimensions from text (Wordscores/Wordfish to LLM positioning).
nodes.relevance: The task the ideological compass performs per query, inheriting the field's validation doctrine.

nodes.label: No parliamentary retrieval/QA benchmark
nodes.summary: Verified absence: no public retrieval test collection or RAG-QA benchmark exists over any contemporary national parliament, and none at all for Italian; BEIR/MTEB/MMTEB contain no parliamentary task.
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG must build its own qrels; releasing them would be a first-of-kind resource.

nodes.label: No parliamentary encoder evaluated on retrieval
nodes.summary: Parliamentary DAPT encoders exist (Knesset-DictaBERT, XLM-R-Parla, ParlBERT, PoliBERTweet) but zero retrieval or embedding-quality evaluations exist across the entire literature.
nodes.relevance: The genuinely open question the embedding ablation answers first.

nodes.label: No verbatim + entailment system
nodes.summary: The literature splits cleanly into substring/membership-only systems and NLI-only systems; no published system combines an enforced verbatim invariant, prose entailment gating, and graph-inherited attribution.
nodes.relevance: Adding a claim auditor would make ParliamentRAG the first system with all three: the headline novelty claim.

nodes.label: No per-party citation quality reporting
nodes.summary: Fair-RAG work measures whose documents get cited, but no published work reports citation precision/recall stratified by political party, demographic group, or topic.
nodes.relevance: Stratifying ALCE-style metrics by party is an open, unclaimed evaluation contribution.

nodes.label: No open Camera XIX corpus besides ParliamentRAG
nodes.summary: ItaParlCorpus stops at legislature XVIII, ParlaMint-IT/ParlaCAP-IT are Senate-only ending ~2022, ParlEE-IT ends 2019: ParliamentRAG's Zenodo/HF release is the only open machine-readable Camera XIX corpus found.
nodes.relevance: Grounds the corpus release as a standalone resource contribution.

nodes.label: MARPOR Italy 2022 missing
nodes.summary: Verified from release notes: the Italian 2022 election is not coded in any MARPOR release through 2025a, so no RILE scores exist for XIX-legislature manifestos.
nodes.relevance: Compass validation must rely on CHES 2024 (plus ParlGov/POPPA) and state this limitation explicitly.

nodes.label: No Italian vote-linked stance dataset
nodes.summary: ParlVote/ConVote have no analogue for Italy or most of Europe; no dataset links speeches to the speaker's roll-call vote for Italian debates.
nodes.relevance: ParliamentRAG's 17.3k roll calls plus speech graph can generate the first one nearly for free.

nodes.label: No externally validated parliamentary RAG compass
nodes.summary: ParliaBench validates political metrics only against corpus-internal centroids with author-assigned labels; no parliamentary system's ideological outputs have been validated against an expert survey at the issue level.
nodes.relevance: The CHES validation protocol would make ParliamentRAG's compass the first.

nodes.label: No internal ablations of ParliamentRAG
nodes.summary: The papers compare only full system vs NotebookLM: contributions of the dual channel, merger weights, quota, and authority score are unquantified (stated limitation).

nodes.label: Underpowered human evaluation
nodes.summary: 6 experts x 67 pairs under 9-way Holm correction had ~51% power at the largest observed effect (d=0.35); Krippendorff alpha -0.20 to 0.08 fails all reliability floors.

nodes.label: No endorsement signal in authority score
nodes.summary: All six authority components are self-activity or attributes; the HITS/PageRank/ethos literature locates authority in what others do toward you, and ParliamentRAG's MENTIONS/CITES edges are unused.
nodes.relevance: The obvious seventh component, to be benchmarked against the simple components before adoption.

nodes.label: Italian parliamentary qrels test collection
nodes.summary: Build the blocking prerequisite: ~50-100 queries from the 51 citizen topics plus paraphrases and harder intents, BEIR-style pooling of top-k from all arms, UMBRELA-style LLM grading with a stratified human audit (kappa >= ~0.5 acceptance), graded 0-3 labels plus party-attributability, frozen on the eval snapshot.
nodes.relevance: Unblocks every retrieval ablation and becomes the first Italian parliamentary retrieval test collection.

nodes.label: Embedding ablation (arms A-D)
nodes.summary: Four arms on frozen chunks and shared qrels: A incumbent text-embedding-3-small + BM25 control; B open multilingual embedders (BGE-M3/mE5); C GPL-adapted retriever on Camera text; D XLM-R-Parla ladder (raw mean-pooled negative control, +SimCSE/TSDAE, +GPL) vs vanilla XLM-R; thresholds recalibrated per arm.
nodes.relevance: First retrieval evaluation of any parliamentary-DAPT model and first public measurement of the closed incumbent on Italian parliamentary text.

nodes.label: Hybrid/BM25 + fusion + reranker ablations
nodes.summary: Channel-contribution matrix (dense-only / graph-only / both / +BM25), RRF vs the convex merger, and a cross-encoder placed upstream of the merger; includes quota on/off (A8) and merger-weight sensitivity (A7) as the zero-cost first steps.
nodes.relevance: Fills the admitted no-internal-ablations gap and measures the relevance price of party balance.

nodes.label: Procedural filtering of interventions
nodes.summary: Tiered filters: chair tagging aligned to ParlaMint speaker types, length/boilerplate rules, a Card-style supervised classifier on existing embeddings, or an index-time LLM rating; then recompute authority for all 387 deputies on the benchmark topics and compare rankings (Kendall tau), with never-presiding deputies as the precision control.
nodes.relevance: Quantifies the BasqueParl effect in the Italian Chamber and either ships the filter or shows the similarity threshold suffices.

nodes.label: Authority external validation (E2-E5)
nodes.summary: Committee-membership hold-out (TREC-Enterprise-style ROC-AUC), convergent validity vs Fowler connectedness / co-voting centrality / MENTIONS in-degree, predictive validation on future relatore/committee/government appointments, and media-coverage correlation.
nodes.relevance: Converts the expert-set authority score into an externally validated construct and a principled way to learn the six weights.

nodes.label: Compass CHES validation protocol (V0-V9)
nodes.summary: Pre-registered criterion validation: >=15 CHES-mapped topics x 3 paraphrases, human axis-to-CHES mapping (kappa >= 0.70), Spearman/Kendall correlations with mixed-effects aggregation (success >= 0.85 expert-grade), discrimination and government-vs-opposition contrast, stability arms, human fragment validation, Wordfish/party-embedding/roll-call convergent baselines, and prior-leakage label-masking plus directional-bias tests.
nodes.relevance: Would make ParliamentRAG the first parliamentary RAG system whose ideological outputs are validated against an expert survey at the issue level.

nodes.label: Fairness calibration regression (E1)
nodes.summary: Mixed-effects regression of per-party retrieval/attribution shares and quality on corpus share, conditioning on per-party relevance mass; slopes tested against 1 (shares) and 0 (quality) with TOST bounds and permutation nulls; extended by counterfactual corpus downsampling (E2) and the quota/coverage 2x2 ablation (E3).
nodes.relevance: The most direct literature-grounded answer to whether the system favors FdI/PD because they are big, distinguishing amplification from quota-driven equalization.

nodes.label: Answer-side balance and tone audit (E4)
nodes.summary: Compare attribution shares vs retrieval shares, per-party quote-valence lopsidedness vs corpus baselines, the full party-centroid similarity vector of each answer, and a closed-book no-RAG control isolating the generator's prior; MODS as optional baseline.
nodes.relevance: Covers the failure mode no retrieval metric sees: equal quotation with unequal framing.

nodes.label: Stage-4.5 Claim Auditor (prose entailment)
nodes.summary: Insert a multilingual-NLI SummaC-style layer between surgeon and assembly: chunk sentences as premises, each non-quote prose sentence as hypothesis, 3-way attributable/extrapolatory/contradictory labels, registry statuses PROSE_SUPPORTED/EXTRAPOLATORY/UNSUPPORTED, EvidenceFirstWriter repair; validated on a 300-pair Italian gold set (E6) and audited against the cosine gate (E2).
nodes.relevance: Completes the verbatim+entailment system and produces the first ALCE-style number for a verbatim-quoting system.

nodes.label: Stratified citation quality by party (E4-cit)
nodes.summary: Compute claim-support, quote-attribution, and coherence metrics stratified by the party each sentence is about and by macro-area, with bootstrap CIs, uniformity tests, and evidence-pool-size regression controls.
nodes.relevance: First stratified citation-quality result in the literature, filling the per-party citation-quality gap.

nodes.label: Cross-family judge panel calibration (X1)
nodes.summary: Run Claude-family, Gemini-family, open-weights, and (as bias positive-control) GPT-family judges plus the 3-family panel on the 67 expert A/B pairs, both orders, x3 reruns; report Cohen's kappa vs expert majority and signed family-bias deltas; PPI-anchor future scaling.
nodes.relevance: Determines whether any automatic evaluator is trustworthy and directly measures same-family bias on a deployed system.

nodes.label: Expert panel redesign (N~112-153, TOST)
nodes.summary: Re-run the human A/B at adequate power: 50+ topics, >=150 expert pairs, two pre-registered directional hypotheses (superiority on Source Relevance/Coverage, TOST non-inferiority on Quality/Clarity), <=4 sheet-defined comparative criteria (BWS/A-B), raw ratings released.
nodes.relevance: Converts 'nothing significant' into two claims matching the system's value proposition, at the sample size the power analysis requires.

nodes.label: Negative-rejection test set (X5)
nodes.summary: 100 unanswerable queries in three tiers (off-domain, near-domain Senate-only, post-cutoff temporal) plus 100 answerable controls, scored deterministically for refusal vs fabrication.
nodes.relevance: Turns the engineering out-of-domain gate (>=10 chunks @ 0.78) into an evaluated safety property with no LLM judge needed.

nodes.label: Italian vote-linked stance dataset
nodes.summary: Replicate ParlVote/ParlVote+ construction over the 17.3k roll calls and linked speeches: speech-level stance labels from the speaker's subsequent vote, with temporal affiliation alignment.

nodes.label: Camera XIX corpus release
